subject: Materials Science
title: Magnesium: Lighter Than Aluminum
description: A micro-lesson that makes Magnesium: Lighter Than Aluminum usable.

hook.text: Pick up a magnesium car wheel and it feels almost hollow — 33% lighter than aluminum.

buildup.text: Magnesium is the lightest structural metal and machines beautifully into complex shapes.

discovery.text: Laptop cases and camera bodies use magnesium alloys for stiffness without weight.

twist.text: Pure magnesium burns white-hot in air — early photographers used it for flash powder.

climax.text: Alloying it with aluminum and zinc tames the fire risk while keeping the weight savings.

punchline.text: The lightest structural metal catches fire if you don't alloy it.

quiz.question: What is a major risk of pure magnesium?
options: It loses strength at room temperature
